web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 2 Structure & Relative Strength
question: Does the price chart confirm institutional accumulation, and where do moving-average support and invalidation levels sit?

epigraph.quote: The tape tells all, if only we know how to read it.
epigraph.author: Jesse Livermore

web_blocks.html: As of the November 13, 2026 close, Arista Networks holds a weekly Stage 2 structure tempered by a daily Stage 3 pullback signal [23]. Shares ended at $197.29 (-4.52% on the day) and stayed above every key moving average [23]. Price sits +2.26% above the 50-day SMA ($192.93) and +5.85% above the 10-week EMA ($186.39) [23]. It also holds +10.78% above the 30-week SMA ($178.09) and +17.89% above the rising 200-day SMA ($167.35) [23]. Because shares sit within +5.85% of the 10-week EMA, the stock is not extended on a weekly basis.

Two internal trend classifiers diverge here, so we reconcile them explicitly. Our daily `facts_US_2026-11-13.json` momentum screen tags ANET as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) because of a `FALLING/FLAT` 50-DMA slope, `5` distribution days in 25 sessions, and `-5.22%` 28-day relative strength inside a `Correction` market (`6` distribution days). By contrast, our weekly `snapshots_US_2026-11-13.json` Weinstein evaluation keeps ANET in **`STAGE_2`** above its rising 30-week SMA ($178.09, +10.78%) and 10-week EMA ($186.39, +5.85%). Because the stricter daily `Stage 3` and `Correction` regime warning governs new-capital timing, we reject buying at CMP. New capital waits for `$183.59–$195.82` support (`WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`) or a confirmed Stage 2 breakout resumption above `$206.63` on expanding volume.

Momentum readings stay healthy rather than overbought. Daily RSI stands at 55.25, 4-hour RSI at 58.68, and weekly RSI at 57.20 [23]. That leaves plenty of room before the >70 overbought zone [23]. Friday's -4.52% dip came on 8.61 million shares, or 1.11x the 30-day average of 7.74 million. That looks like normal profit-taking near Pivot R1 ($201.89) rather than institutional selling. Still, 14-day ATR is $11.99 (6.1% of share price) and 1-year beta is 2.42. Because daily swings run wide, patient limit bids near support beat market orders.

web_blocks.title: 8.2 Relative Strength Against a Market Correction & Stage 4 Peers

web_blocks.html: Market context matters as much as the stock's own chart. U.S. equities sit in a `Correction (below 50-DMA, above 200-DMA)` regime. Only 50.0% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-DMA, 45.2% sit above their 200-DMA, and the index logged 6 distribution days in 25 sessions [27]. CBOE options flow shows steady hedging, with a 0.85 total put/call ratio, 0.63 equity put/call, and 0.96 index put/call [27]. Meanwhile, SPY faces a nearby call wall at $769 and put wall at $763 [27]. Against that weak tape, CSCO ($95.64), HPE ($48.29), CLS ($240.34), NVDA ($162.85), and AVGO ($347.01) have all fallen into `STAGE_4` (`CAP_REJECTED`). ANET holds +17.89% above its 200-day SMA and just -9.25% off its $217.41 52-week high, proving real institutional relative strength.

web_blocks.title: 8.3 Institutional Ownership, Short Interest & Options Convexity

web_blocks.html: Ownership data backs up the chart's stability. Institutions hold 74.94% of Arista shares, while insiders own 16.66%—led by co-founders Andy Bechtolsheim and Kenneth Duda plus CEO Jayshree Ullal [22]. That stake creates strong long-term alignment [22]. Short interest is low at 12.03 million shares, or 1.14% of the 1.05 billion share float and 1.92 days to cover [22]. Bears are clearly not pressing a structural short bet [22]. In options, 30-day implied volatility is 57.1% versus 86.2% 20-day realized volatility (`IV_CHEAP`). Investors wanting defined-risk upside during a market correction can use the September 17, 2027 $180 LEAPS Call (306 DTE, 0.70 delta, ~$51.90 mid). That contract caps max loss at $5,190, breaks even at $231.90, and delivers 69% stock-replacement exposure.

book_paragraphs: A strong business can still be a painful stock if you buy it while big institutions are heading for the exits. So after checking the business and the valuation, we turn to the tape. As of November 13, 2026, Arista Networks holds a weekly Stage 2 structure above its 30-week average, even though its daily chart flashes a Stage 3 pullback signal inside a broader market correction.

Consider the backdrop. The S&P 500 is below its 50-day moving average with six distribution days—sessions where institutional sellers dump stock on heavy volume—over the last five weeks. Half the market sits below its 50-day average. Yet Arista closed at $197.29, still 2.26% above its 50-day average ($192.93), 5.85% above its 10-week exponential average ($186.39), and 17.89% above its rising 200-day average ($167.35). Compare that with Cisco, HPE, Celestica, NVIDIA, and Broadcom, every single one of which has slipped into a Stage 4 downtrend.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Support Shelves and Volatility
paragraphs: Friday's 4.52% pullback looks dramatic on a headline, but the volume tells a calmer story: 8.61 million shares traded, just 1.11 times the 30-day average of 7.74 million. Real institutional liquidation shows up on two-to-three-times normal volume. Here, buyers simply paused near $201.89 resistance after a 14.2% weekly post-earnings run, leaving daily RSI at a healthy 55.25 and weekly RSI at 57.20.

That said, Arista is not a sleepy utility. Its 14-day Average True Range is $11.99—meaning a 6% daily swing is routine noise—and its one-year beta is 2.42. That is why we anchor our buy zone between $183.59 and $195.82, right where the 50-day, 10-week, and 4-hour 50-period averages cluster, and place our structural stop below the 30-week shelf ($178.09) at $172.09. If Arista breaks $172.09 on a closing basis, the Stage 2 thesis is broken and we step aside. Now let us weigh both sides of the investment debate and build a concrete action plan.

book_subsections.title: Options Flow, Ownership Alignment, and the LEAPS Alternative
paragraphs: Outside the equity chart, two other gauges confirm that Arista's institutional backing remains steady. First, insiders still own 16.66% of the company alongside 74.94% institutional ownership, while short interest sits at just 1.14% of the float—fewer than two days of average volume to cover. Bears are not pressing a structural short bet here.

Second, in the options market, 30-day implied volatility is 57.1% compared with 86.2% actual 20-day realized volatility. In plain terms, option premiums are relatively inexpensive compared with how fast the stock has actually been moving. For an investor who wants upside participation without risking $19,729 per hundred shares during a market correction, a September 17, 2027 $180 LEAPS Call—trading near $51.90 per share, or $5,190 per contract—controls roughly 69% of the upside of 100 shares while capping worst-case loss at the $5,190 upfront debit and decaying at just $7.50 per day.

book_subsections.title: Why Market Regime Dictates Patience Over Chasing
paragraphs: Even when a single stock passes every technical test, you never trade it in a vacuum. On November 13, 2026, CBOE equity put/call sat at 0.63 and total put/call at 0.85, while SPY faced heavy call-option resistance at $769 and put support at $763. With the S&P 500 below its 50-day average and six distribution days on the board, breakouts fail more often than they run. That is why we respect Arista's Stage 2 relative strength without paying up above $201.89 resistance—letting pullbacks toward the 50-day ($192.93) and 10-week ($186.39) averages come to us.

book_subsections.title: Using the 4-Hour, Daily, and Weekly Moving-Average Stack
paragraphs: When timing an entry in a high-beta leader like Arista (beta 2.42, ATR $11.99), aligning three timeframes keeps you from buying into short-term exhaustion. On the weekly chart, the 10-week EMA sits at $186.39 and the 30-week SMA—our primary Stage 2 shelf—sits at $178.09. On the daily chart, the 50-day SMA sits at $192.93 and the 200-day SMA sits at $167.35. On the 4-hour chart, the 20-EMA ($187.57) and 50-SMA ($183.37) frame the exact intraday dip-buying pocket.
Notice how cleanly those levels stack between $183.59 and $195.82. Placing limit orders inside that confluence band lets you buy right at institutional support rather than chasing a 14% weekly spike.

book_subsections.title: Volume Dry-Ups, Distribution Days, and Recognizing Institutional Support
paragraphs: How will you know over the next few weeks whether our $183.59–$195.82 support zone is holding? Watch volume on red days versus green days. Healthy Stage 2 pullbacks occur on shrinking volume—ideally below the 30-day average of 7.74 million shares—showing that long-term institutions are sitting tight rather than dumping stock. If ANET tests the 50-day average ($192.93) or 10-week average ($186.39) on quiet volume and bounces back above $201.89 on heavy volume, that confirms the next leg higher; if it slices through $172.09 on heavy volume, the tape is telling you to step aside.

book_subsections.title: Respecting the $172.09 Line in the Sand
paragraphs: Technical discipline exists to protect you from your own conviction when the facts change before the headlines do. Placing your structural stop at $172.09—half an ATR below the 30-week moving average at $178.09—gives the stock room to breathe through normal 6% daily volatility while guaranteeing that you never ride a Stage 2 leader down into a Stage 4 breakdown like Cisco, NVIDIA, or Broadcom.

book_subsections.title: How Institutional Flow Shapes the Post-Earnings Tape
paragraphs: After a 58.5% year-over-year revenue quarter, institutions rarely exit a true Stage 2 leader in one day; instead, they accumulate shares on controlled pullbacks toward the 50-day and 10-week moving averages. Watching how ANET behaves around $192.93 and $186.39 over the coming sessions will tell you whether pension funds and growth managers are defending the post-earnings gap or letting broader market distribution pull the stock down toward its 30-week shelf at $178.09.
